close_reason: Landed in 0714edb alongside .48. The is_valid_sha256_hex private helper had no remaining callers after .48 typed expected_sha256, and the rustdoc on hex_digest_eq lost its mention of that helper. The two findings landed as a single coordinated change per the bead description's recommendation.
description: crate-jmap-base-client/src/blob.rs:414-416 keeps is_valid_sha256_hex as a free helper used only by download_blob's expected_sha256 validation (blob.rs:387-391). After bd:JMAP-v9py.13 promoted the SERVER side (BlobUploadResponse.sha256) to typed Sha256, this validator survives only because the CALLER side (DownloadBlobParams.expected_sha256) is still &str — see the partnered finding on JMAP-6r7c.48. If .48 is resolved by switching expected_sha256 to Option<&Sha256>, the entire is_valid_sha256_hex function becomes dead code AND the to_ascii_lowercase normalize step (blob.rs:396) disappears AND the InvalidArgument("expected_sha256 is not 64-char hex") branch is unreachable. The function itself is also documented as 'Returns true if s is exactly 64 hex characters (uppercase or lowercase)' but its only caller normalises to lowercase via to_ascii_lowercase immediately after — so the helper's case-insensitive check is doing work that no caller actually relies on. Recommendation: track is_valid_sha256_hex removal as a follow-up to .48; do NOT delete it independently because the &str API is published. The two findings should land together as a single coordinated change at the next minor-version-with-typed-API bump.
title: is_valid_sha256_hex still gates download_blob expected_sha256 path; redundant if expected_sha256 becomes typed
